player_action: I bull rush the orc off the cliff.
game_state: Medium fighter, no Improved Bull Rush, orc adjacent standing 5 ft from a cliff edge.
correct_ruling: Bull rush is a standard action (or part of a charge); you move into the defender's square, provoking AoOs from all threatening creatures including the defender (without Improved Bull Rush), then make opposed Strength checks with size modifiers; if you win you push the defender back 5 ft plus 5 ft per 5 points you beat it by (limited by your movement), so a push off the cliff is possible.
common_wrong_rulings: Pushes only 5 ft no matter what.

game_state: Medium fighter vs Large ogre, no Improved Trip, armed with a longsword.
correct_ruling: Tripping is an unarmed melee touch attack, so without Improved Trip (and with a longsword, not a trip weapon) it provokes an attack of opportunity from the ogre. If it hits, make an opposed check: your Strength against the ogre's Strength or Dexterity (whichever is higher), with the Large ogre getting +4 for being one size larger. If you lose, the ogre may immediately try to trip you in return.
common_wrong_rulings: Trip isn't a combat option in 3.5.

player_action: I disarm the bandit's longsword using my dagger.
game_state: Fighter with dagger (light) vs bandit with longsword (one-handed).
correct_ruling: Disarm: provokes an AoO from the target (without Improved Disarm), then opposed attack rolls; light weapon takes -4, two-handed weapon gets +4. If you fail, the defender may try to disarm you in return.

player_action: I overrun the goblin to get past it.
game_state: Medium fighter, goblin (Small) in the path.
correct_ruling: Overrun is done as part of a move (a standard action during movement or as part of a charge); the defender can choose to avoid you; if it blocks, opposed Strength checks (Dex/Str), size modifiers apply; success knocks the defender prone and you move through.
common_wrong_rulings: The defender can't choose to avoid.

game_state: Fighter with greataxe vs wizard's quarterstaff (held).
correct_ruling: Sundering a held weapon is a melee attack that provokes an AoO from the holder (without Improved Sunder) and uses opposed attack rolls; if you win, roll damage against the weapon's hardness and hit points (wooden quarterstaff hardness 5).
common_wrong_rulings: You just roll damage against the staff with no check.

player_action: I'm a dwarf, so I'm basically immune to being tripped, right?
game_state: Dwarf fighter being tripped by an orc.
correct_ruling: No; dwarves have stability, which gives +4 on ability checks to resist bull rush or trip while standing on the ground — a bonus, not immunity.

player_action: I want to trip the gelatinous cube.
correct_ruling: The trip rules give the defender +4 for every leg beyond two and note that some creatures (for example legless or flying ones) can't be tripped; an ooze has no legs, so it can't be tripped. Where a creature's anatomy is ambiguous, the DM decides.
confidence_note: SRD says the defender gets +4 for each leg beyond two and that some creatures (e.g. oozes, legless) can't be tripped — wording of the latter not verified.

player_action: I'm charging the orc. I get +2 to hit, right? And what's the downside?
game_state: Fighter 30 ft from orc, clear straight path.
correct_ruling: Charge: move up to twice speed in a straight line to an adjacent square, +2 on the attack roll and -2 to AC until your next turn. You must move at least 10 ft and the path must be unobstructed.

player_action: I want to disarm the otyugh of its tentacle.
correct_ruling: You can't disarm natural weapons or body parts; the disarm rule targets held objects. Severing body parts is not part of the SRD combat rules; the DM decides any called-shot style effect, but RAW it isn't available.
common_wrong_rulings: Disarm with a penalty removes the eye.

player_action: I use Aid Another to help my rogue friend hit the orc.
game_state: Fighter adjacent to the orc, rogue attacking it.
correct_ruling: Aid another is a standard action; attack AC 10; on success your ally gets +2 on their next attack roll against that opponent (or +2 AC against that opponent's next attack).

player_action: I'm feinting the ogre with Bluff so my rogue can sneak attack.
game_state: Rogue, Bluff +8, attacking an ogre (Giant type, Sense Motive +2, BAB +3) together with a rogue ally.
correct_ruling: Feint is a standard action: Bluff opposed by Sense Motive (target adds BAB). Success: target loses its Dex bonus against your next melee attack, which must be made on or before your next turn — only for you, not your ally. Against a nonhumanoid you take -4; against an Int 1-2 creature, -8.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Special Attacks > Feint; Skills > Bluff
confidence_note: Ogre is a giant (not humanoid), so -4 applies; graders shouldn't require that.

player_action: I charge the orc, but it's okay that I have to go around this pillar — the rule is just 'move toward it'.
correct_ruling: Charge requires moving in a direct line to the closest space from which you can attack, with no obstacles (difficult terrain or creatures) in the path; you can't charge around the pillar.
